CAMWS, a regional learned society serving scholars, educators, and students of Greek, Latin, and classical antiquity (national membership of ~1,100), seeks proposals for a full redesign and redevelopment of its website. The project includes a public-facing redesign, member portal functionality (login, renewals, directory), conference registration with abstract submission and payment processing, and a modern CMS suited to a small nonprofit staff.



Full scope includes visual design and a design system, WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility compliance, content migration with URL redirects, staff training and documentation, and post-launch support. Vendors should have demonstrated experience with nonprofit/membership organizations, ideally academic or scholarly associations, and familiarity with membership platforms, conference registration, and PCI-compliant payment processing.



Proposals must include an executive summary, team bios, a portfolio of comparable work, technical approach, milestone-based timeline, migration plan, three client references, and an itemized cost proposal (development, hosting/licensing, ongoing support).



Please see the full RFP in the PDF attached to this site.

   SENIOR BACKEND ENGINEER: OPTIMIZE AUTOMATION SYSTEM
   
   We're a Los Angeles leasing company . Our whole operation runs on 14 automations on Railway: tour confirmation texts, driver schedules, owner access texts, application intake, DocuSign contracts, invoicing, and a sync between Monday.com (our CRM) and Quo/OpenPhone (our phones). About 57,000 lines across Node.js and Python, several using the Claude API to read customer replies and write reports. It works and it runs our day. But it was built fast, one fix at a time, and it shows: - The same business rules are written in 5 places in two languages, and they drift apart. - 11 separate Monday connections and 25 files talking to our phone API. Every service polls on a timer, and we're using about 3 times Monday's daily API limit. - AI costs are high: full AI agents run for routine reports, with no caching. - One test file across 14 services. No version history, no staging environment, and deploys come from a laptop. - Mistakes are found by our team after customers see them. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Put everything in GitHub with CI, plus a staging environment that uses test boards and a test phone line. - Build one shared library: a single client each for Monday, Quo and Gmail, with rate limits, retries and call counting, and a single rules module, used by every service. - Replace polling with webhooks wherever the APIs allow, and cache the rest. - Cut AI spend: use plain code where a rule will do, cache prompts, and match each task to the right model. - Turn our written rules and our long list of past mistakes into automated tests, so a fix can't break an earlier one. - Add a simple dashboard: what each service did, what it cost, and what failed. - Then stay on part-time (about 5-10 hours a week) to review changes and handle incidents.
